problem: Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture : a conjectured local–global principle for linear ordinary differential equations
missing_details: Expression of the problem as the linear differential system dv/dz = A(z)v with A an n×n matrix of algebraic functions over algebraic number coefficients
Definition of a full set of algebraic function solutions as existence of a fundamental matrix
Description of the p-curvature endomorphism for the mod p reduction of the connection
Condition quantified as holding for almost all prime numbers p of the base number field
Over finite fields: algebraic solutions mod p and vanishing of p-curvature
Equivalence: vanishing p-curvature mod p implies existence of algebraic solutions over the original field
refined_question: Let K be a number field and let E be an n-dimensional vector bundle over the projective line P^1_K equipped with an integrable algebraic connection ∇ defined by the linear differential system dv/dz = A(z)v with A(z) a matrix in M_n(K(z)). For a nonzero prime ideal p of the ring of integers O_K at which (E, ∇) has good reduction, let ψ_p denote the p-curvature endomorphism of the reduced connection over the finite field O_K/p. The Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture asks: If ψ_p = 0 for almost all prime ideals p of O_K, does it follow that (E, ∇) admits a full set of algebraic solutions over the algebraic closure of K(z) (equivalently, that its monodromy representation has finite image)?
justification: The name 'Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture' indicates a conjecture by Grothendieck and refined by Katz about p-curvature but omits details about the underlying differential system, the notion of algebraic solutions, and the precise local-to-global condition. The refined question explicitly defines the number field K, the vector bundle and connection, the p-curvature, and the equivalence between vanishing p-curvature for almost all primes and the existence of a full set of algebraic solutions.
